title: Temporal amplitude–interval phase inconsistency failed to improve cross-cohort PPG respiratory-error prediction
abstract: Temporal amplitude–interval respiratory phase inconsistency did not improve transferable prediction of PPG respiratory-rate errors exceeding3breaths/min under fixed ridge logistic models. BIDMC-trained models evaluated on independent CapnoBase had Brier scores0.136418 baseline and0.137893 augmented, a gain of-0.001476 [-0.002605, -0.000445]. Reverse transfer gave0.194200 and0.194195, gain0.000005 [-0.000892, 0.000939]. Intervals are95% paired target-record bootstrap conditional on fitted source models. This exploratory negative result does not exclude useful phase information under other estimators.
